chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, and a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Abu Ubaydah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

When the one in Ihram attains the hunted prey, and cannot find what he can use to expiate from the place where he attained the prey, the value of its penalty should be assessed in dirhams from the livestock; then the dirhams should be assessed as food for each poor person, being half a sa'; so if he is not able to provide the food, he should fast one day for each half sa'.

key_terms.الْمُحْرِمُ: The pilgrim in the state of Ihram
key_terms.صَاعٍ: Sa' (a traditional unit of volume for food)

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for killing game while in Ihram if the specific sacrificial animal is unavailable?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the graduated hierarchy of expiation (kaffarah) for hunting violations during Ihram, establishing a fallback mechanism when the primary sacrifice of livestock is unavailable. It reflects the Shia juristic principle of converting the value of the animal into food for the poor, and finally into fasting, ensuring the penalty remains accessible regardless of the pilgrim's financial or logistical circumstances. This progression underscores the flexibility in Shia fiqh to maintain the spiritual integrity of the Hajj ritual through practical, tiered compensations.
